summary: This function transforms any string into a URL-safe slug by converting it to lowercase, removing accents and special characters, replacing spaces with hyphens, and cleaning up extra hyphens. It handles common cases like camelCase input and ensures the output is clean and web-friendly.

explanations.17: This regex looks for a lowercase letter or digit followed immediately by an uppercase letter (like the 'c' and 'C' in camelCase) and inserts a hyphen between them, converting camelCase to kebab-case.
explanations.19: NFD is a Unicode normalization form that breaks apart accented characters into their base letter plus separate accent marks, which the next line then removes.
explanations.20: The Unicode range \u0300-\u036f contains all the accent marks (diacritics) that were separated out by the normalize() call, so this removes them entirely.
explanations.21: This removes any character that isn't a lowercase letter, digit, space, or hyphen — essentially stripping out punctuation and symbols.
explanations.23: After replacing spaces with hyphens, you might end up with multiple hyphens in a row (like 'hello--world'), so this collapses them back down to single hyphens.
